quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign with white background and red and black markings. It tells drivers what traffic laws apply in this area. This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What do white lines on a roadway do?

options.text: Separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.
Separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means you cannot pass. A dashed white line means you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Avoid making sudden moves, as doing so could cause a skid.
Travel on the shoulder to be out of the way of traffic.
Use only the rear brake because the front brake is ineffective on slippery surfaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid making sudden moves, as doing so could cause a skid.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, sudden changes in speed or direction can cause a skid. Make smooth, gradual movements when speeding up, shifting gears, turning, or braking.

questions.question: Which of the following checks do you NOT need to do before riding your motorcycle?

options.text: Check that your tires have proper air pressure.
Check that the oil levels are safe.
Look under the motorcycle for leaks.
Check that the paint is shiny.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the paint is shiny.
questions.explanation: Before any trip, check your tire pressure, wear, and tread. Check your oil and fluid levels. Look under the motorcycle for oil or gas leaks. Paint shine is not a safety concern.

questions.question: What about hearing protection?

options.text: Is not needed when the rider is wearing a helmet.
Is only recommended for long trips.
Should be used on all rides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be used on all rides.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing, even when wearing a helmet. Use hearing protection on every ride.

questions.question: Which statement is NOT a benefit of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You will have time to react to hazards.
You will have space to maneuver.
You will have more time to accelerate when entering a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will have more time to accelerate when entering a curve.
questions.explanation: Keeping space around your motorcycle gives you time to react and room to maneuver if someone else makes a mistake. Extra acceleration time in a curve is not a safety benefit.

questions.question: Experienced riders use a system called SIPDE. What does the "I" stand for?
questions.explanation: SIPDE stands for Scan, Identify, Predict, Decide, and Execute. This system helps riders make safe decisions while riding.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
You may go through the intersection carefully.
You must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red traffic light. You must stop completely and wait for a signal that allows you to turn.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast can cause a rider to:

options.text: Accidentally move into another lane of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Accidentally move into another lane of traffic.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast may cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road. Slow down before entering a turn or curve.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks affect a rider's ability to operate safely?
questions.explanation: Even one alcoholic drink can harm your ability to ride safely. Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: How long does a pre-ride inspection take?

options.text: It must be done by a certified mechanic.

questions.explanation: You should inspect your motorcycle before every ride. This inspection takes only a few minutes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will enter the roadway ahead.
Stop completely, then go when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: Where should a passenger sit on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Passengers must sit behind the operator and hold onto the operator's waist or hips. They can also hold onto handgrips if the motorcycle has them. Passengers should never sit sidesaddle.

questions.question: What color are service signs?
questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are located. These include rest areas, gas stations, restaurants, and hospitals.

questions.question: How are convex mirrors different from regular mirrors?

options.text: They show a narrower view of the road.
They show a wider view of the road.
They show a clearer view of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They show a wider view of the road.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors provide a wider view than flat mirrors. However, they can make vehicles behind you look farther away than they really are.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's stopping power comes from the front brake?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the total stopping power.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns drivers that a railroad crossing is coming up.

questions.question: What does your steering feel like if your front tire goes flat?
questions.explanation: If steering suddenly feels heavy, your front tire may be flat. Stop and check your tires right away.

questions.question: When being passed, should you move to the far side of your lane?

options.text: Yes, you will be farther from the passing vehicle.
No, it may cause the other driver to return to your lane too soon.
It does not matter for safety reasons.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it may cause the other driver to return to your lane too soon.
questions.explanation: Do not move to the far side of your lane when being passed. This may signal the passing driver to return to your lane too early.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift located?
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is located in front of the left footrest. The rider operates it with the left foot.

questions.question: Before riding with a passenger, you should tell them to:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle before you do.
Sit as far back as possible.
Hold on firmly to your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold on firmly to your waist, hips, or belt.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to wait until after you start the engine before getting on. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you and hold on firmly to your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle properly, you should:

options.text: Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Use your arms to hold up your body.
Keep your knees against the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can easily reach all controls. Keep your arms slightly bent and use them to steer, not to support your body. Press your knees against the gas tank to help balance during turns.

questions.question: When riding in a group, motorcycles should generally be arranged in:
questions.explanation: A staggered pattern is best for group riding. It keeps riders close together while giving each rider enough space. Use a single-file line when turning, entering a highway, or exiting a highway.

questions.question: Which of these is a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Poor traction can occur on wet, snowy, icy, or muddy pavement; gravel roads; lane markings; and steel plates or utility hole covers.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance if:
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance if your motorcycle needs more time to stop, if you can't see around the vehicle ahead, or if traffic is heavy and other vehicles might cut in front of you.
